title: Introduce rhythm-based token scale for micro-interactions, chart overlays, and dense lists
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Our current token scale evolved ad-hoc across components, leading to inconsistent spacing, radii, and shadow volumes in dense surfaces (tables, compact lists, chart overlays) and for micro-interactions (press/hover). Goal: define a simple rhythm-based token scale (spacings, corner radii, shadow spread/elevation, and a micro-interaction outline system) that harmonizes visual cadence across compact and regular density surfaces while preserving accessibility contrast and hit target guidance.
acceptance_criteria: A 4-step rhythmic scale is documented (base unit x, 1x, 1.5x, 2x) for spacing and radii with explicit mapping to component use-cases (buttons, chips, table rows, chart overlays).
Shadow/elevation presets updated to three micro-elevation levels with measured luminance and contrast impact and guidance for when to use blur vs spread.
Micro-interaction states (hover/press/focus) standardized with token references and accessible outlines (minimum contrast guidance).
Figma token file updated and synced to code token JSON; at least 10 components updated in the component library with visual QA signoff.
Performance: token renames do not increase bundle size by more than 1% after build-time pruning; rollout plan includes codemod for 2 major repos.
design_assets: Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/rhythm-tokens (draft frames: Rhythm Tokens / Compact Surfaces)
comments: 2025-02-14 Maya Chen: Initial proposal uploaded to Confluence. Framing the problem around dense surfaces and micro-interactions after design review with PM. Asked ENG to evaluate token mapping impact on component library.

2025-02-15 Diego Ramos: Pulled early token draft into Figma. Noted that chart overlays need a dedicated z-elevation token to avoid collision with tooltip shadows. Added example overlays for time-series charts.
2025-02-16 Priya Patel (PM): Approved scope for cycle 2025-W07. Requested telemetry hooks to track components migrated and a metric for visual regressions (appearance tests).
2025-02-17 Justin Kim (Eng): Ran a quick bundle analysis—proposed token prefixing strategy to avoid doubling keys. Raised question about codemod complexity for legacy CSS variables.

2025-02-18 Design review: Decided on base unit x = 4px for rhythm calculations; adopted 1.5x as a primary compact step for button height in dense rows. Action: Diego to update Figma and prepare token export.

2025-02-19 Accessibility review (Liam O'Connor): Outline contrast requirement for focus states set to 4.5:1 against immediate background. Suggested swapping one micro-elevation to use subtle stroke rather than shadow for low-contrast backgrounds.
decisions: Adopt 4-step rhythm scale based on 4px base: 1x (4px), 1.5x (6px), 2x (8px), 3x (12px) — used for spacing and radius tokens.
Introduce micro-elevation tokens: micro-1 (0.6 blur, 4% opacity), micro-2 (1.2 blur, 8% opacity), micro-3 (2.4 blur, 12% opacity) with explicit use-cases for overlays, cards, and pressed states.
Define chart-overlay token z-elevation that sits above tooltip layer but below modals; overlay shadows should be softer (lower spread) to avoid visual clutter.
Standardize interaction outlines: use token outline.focus-strong for keyboard focus and outline.touch for touch presses; both must meet contrast guidance.
tradeoffs: Choosing a 4px base simplifies math across the product but requires a handful of component dimension updates; acceptable for UX consistency.
Using subtle strokes instead of extra shadow for low-contrast backgrounds reduces perceived depth but improves legibility and reduces GPU work on lower-end devices.
A compact 1.5x step in heights means some existing components will need minor layout adjustments—short-term dev cost for long-term rhythm harmony.
